def: Behaviour by an employee that breaks the employer's rules or the employee's obligations.

formal.ex: Any act of [[misconduct]] may give rise to disciplinary action in accordance with this policy.

everyday.ex: We can't keep turning a blind eye to this kind of [[bad behaviour]].
everyday.ex_us: We can't keep turning a blind eye to this kind of [[bad behavior]].

note_fr: Indénombrable : « an act of misconduct », jamais « a misconduct ». Ne traduisez pas « faute » par « fault » (défaut, responsabilité : « it's my fault ») ni par « mistake » (erreur involontaire).

def: In French law, misconduct serious enough to justify dismissal, but not serious enough to deprive the employee of notice and severance pay.

formal.ex: The tribunal held that the facts amounted to [[ordinary misconduct]] only, so that notice and severance pay remained due.

everyday.ex: It's [[misconduct that isn't gross misconduct]], so he keeps his notice and his severance.

collocations: to be downgraded to ordinary misconduct
note_fr: « Simple misconduct » se comprend, mais « ordinary misconduct » est plus naturel. Ni le Royaume-Uni ni les États-Unis ne connaissent cette gradation à trois niveaux : on y oppose seulement « misconduct » et « gross misconduct ».

explain.written: Ordinary misconduct (faute simple) is misconduct that constitutes a real and serious cause for dismissal while leaving the employee's entitlement to notice and severance pay intact.
explain.spoken: It's the lowest level of misconduct that can still justify dismissal - the employee goes, but with notice and severance.

def: Misconduct so serious that the employee cannot be kept on, even for the notice period.

formal.ex: Theft, violence and serious breaches of safety rules are regarded as [[gross misconduct]].

everyday.ex: Shouting at a client once is bad, but I'm not sure it's [[serious misconduct]].

collocations: to be dismissed for gross misconduct
note_fr: « Gross » /ɡrəʊs/ rime avec « close », pas avec « boss ». En France, la faute grave prive le salarié du préavis et de l'indemnité de licenciement, mais non de l'indemnité de congés payés. Au Royaume-Uni, « gross misconduct » justifie un « summary dismissal » ; la notion est proche, mais reste définie par le contrat et la jurisprudence.

explain.written: Faute grave is misconduct of such seriousness that the employee cannot remain in the business even during the notice period; it deprives the employee of notice and severance pay.
explain.spoken: It's roughly what you'd call gross misconduct: the employee leaves straight away, with no notice and no severance.

term.uk: wilful misconduct with intent to harm
term.us: wilful misconduct with intent to harm

def: In French law, the most serious degree of misconduct: an act committed with the intention of harming the employer.

formal.uk: wilful misconduct committed with intent to harm the employer
formal.us: willful misconduct committed with intent to harm the employer
formal.ex: The Company considers that the deliberate deletion of client files constitutes [[wilful misconduct committed with intent to harm the employer]].
formal.ex_us: The Company considers that the deliberate deletion of client files constitutes [[willful misconduct committed with intent to harm the employer]].

everyday.uk: deliberately trying to damage the company
everyday.us: deliberately trying to damage the company
everyday.ex: To call it faute lourde, we'd have to show he was [[deliberately trying to damage the company]].

collocations: to hold the employee liable for the loss
note_fr: Orthographe : « wilful » (UK), « willful » (US). L'intention de nuire doit être prouvée ; c'est le seul cas où l'employeur peut engager la responsabilité pécuniaire du salarié. Aucun équivalent exact en droit britannique ou américain.

explain.written: Faute lourde is misconduct committed with intent to harm the employer; in addition to the consequences of faute grave, it allows the employer to seek damages from the employee.
explain.spoken: It's the top of the scale: not just serious misconduct, but something done on purpose to hurt the company.

def: A measure taken by the employer in response to an employee's misconduct, from a warning to dismissal.

formal.ex: No [[disciplinary sanction]] may be imposed on an employee without the employee being informed in writing of the complaints against him or her.

everyday.ex: If it happens again, we'll have to take [[disciplinary action]].

collocations: to take disciplinary action against someone
note_fr: « Sanction » est un faux ami partiel : le verbe « to sanction » signifie aussi « autoriser, approuver ». Pour dire « sanctionner un salarié », préférez « to discipline someone » ou « to take disciplinary action against someone ».

def: To decide formally that an employee will be given a disciplinary measure.

formal.ex: The employer may not [[impose a sanction]] more than one month after the date of the meeting.

everyday.ex: She [[was disciplined]] for sharing her password with a temp.

collocations: to decide on the appropriate sanction
note_fr: On ne « pronounce » pas une sanction en anglais (« to pronounce » = prononcer un mot). « To discipline someone » est le verbe courant ; « to punish » appartient plutôt au registre moral ou pénal.

def: The series of steps an employer must follow before disciplining an employee.

formal.ex: The Company reserves the right to commence [[disciplinary proceedings]] in respect of any breach of these rules.

everyday.ex: Once we start [[the disciplinary process]], we have to see it through properly.

collocations: at each stage of the procedure
note_fr: « Procedure » = les règles à suivre ; « proceedings » = la procédure effectivement engagée contre quelqu'un. Au Royaume-Uni, « a disciplinary » s'emploie familièrement comme nom : « he's got a disciplinary on Friday ».

def: To do something that the employer's rules forbid, or fail to do something they require.

formal.uk: to be in breach of the Company's rules
formal.us: to be in breach of the Company's rules
formal.ex: An employee who smokes on the production floor [[is in breach of the Company's rules]].

everyday.ex: He knew perfectly well he [[was breaking the rules]].

informal.ex: Everyone [[bends the rules]] a little on expenses, but this went far beyond that.

collocations: a serious breach of the rules
a breach of health and safety rules
note_fr: Évitez « to infringe the regulation » (calque). « Regulations » désigne plutôt des textes réglementaires ; pour le règlement intérieur d'une entreprise, dites « company rules », « works rules » ou « the disciplinary rules ». « To bend the rules » = prendre des libertés avec la règle, sans la violer franchement.

def: A first, spoken warning that an employee's conduct or performance must improve.

formal.ex: A [[verbal warning]] will normally be given for a first instance of minor misconduct.

everyday.ex: I've had [[a quiet word]] with him about his timekeeping; let's see if it helps.

collocations: to give someone a verbal warning
to have a word with someone
note_fr: En droit français, une simple observation orale n'est pas une sanction ; l'avertissement suppose un écrit. « To have a word with someone » = lui parler brièvement pour le rappeler à l'ordre ; à ne pas confondre avec « to have words with someone » (se disputer).

def: A formal letter telling an employee that their conduct or performance is unacceptable and what will happen if it does not improve.

formal.ex: This letter constitutes a formal [[written warning]], a copy of which will be placed on your personnel file.

everyday.ex: He's already had [[a written warning]] for the same thing.
everyday.ex_us: He's already had [[a write-up]] for the same thing.

note_fr: Aux États-Unis, « to write someone up » / « a write-up » désigne couramment l'avertissement écrit. « Advertisement » est un faux ami : c'est une publicité ou une annonce, jamais un avertissement.

def: The last formal warning before dismissal, given after earlier warnings or for a serious first offence.

formal.ex: Any further misconduct while this [[final written warning]] remains in force is likely to result in your dismissal.

everyday.ex: She's on a [[final warning]], so one more incident and that's it.

informal.ex: Frankly, this is his [[last chance]].

collocations: to be on a final warning
to issue a final written warning
note_fr: Notion surtout britannique : la gradation « verbal - written - final written warning » découle des bonnes pratiques (code Acas), non d'une obligation légale. En France, aucun nombre d'avertissements n'est exigé avant un licenciement. Dites « to be on a final warning », pas « to have a last warning ».

def: To give an employee a formal warning.

formal.ex: The manager may [[issue a warning]] only after hearing the employee's explanation.

everyday.ex: We [[gave him a warning]] back in March and nothing has changed.

collocations: to be issued with a warning (UK)
to warn someone about their conduct
note_fr: « To notify a warning » est un calque : on dit « to issue a warning » ou « to give someone a warning ». Au Royaume-Uni, « to be issued with a warning » ; aux États-Unis, « to be issued a warning », sans préposition.

def: A formal expression of disapproval addressed to an employee, more solemn than a simple warning.

formal.ex: The sanction imposed is a [[formal reprimand]], which will be recorded on your file.

everyday.ex: His manager [[pulled him up]] on the tone of his emails.
everyday.ex_us: His manager [[called him out]] on the tone of his emails.

informal.ex: She got [[a telling-off]] from the site manager for not wearing her helmet.
informal.ex_us: She got [[a talking-to]] from the site manager for not wearing her helmet.

note_fr: « Blame » n'est pas un blâme : « to blame someone » = tenir quelqu'un pour responsable. Le blâme français se rend par « reprimand » ; « censure » est réservé aux contextes institutionnels ou professionnels (ordres, parlement).

fr: avertissement encore en vigueur (inscrit au dossier)
def: A warning that is still in force and can therefore be taken into account if there is further misconduct.

formal.ex: This warning will [[remain in force]] for a period of twelve months from the date of this letter.

everyday.ex: The warning [[stays on file]] for a year, then it's disregarded.

collocations: to be disregarded for disciplinary purposes
note_fr: « Live » se prononce ici /laɪv/. Au Royaume-Uni, un avertissement expiré est dit « spent » ou « lapsed ». En France, aucune sanction antérieure de plus de trois ans ne peut être invoquée à l'appui d'une nouvelle sanction.

def: A sanction that consists in taking money from the employee, such as a fine or a deduction from pay.

formal.ex: French law prohibits any fine or other [[financial penalty]] imposed on an employee by way of sanction.

everyday.ex: You can't [[dock his pay]] because he broke the scanner.

note_fr: « To dock » = retenir sur le salaire. En France, les amendes et sanctions pécuniaires sont interdites ; ne pas payer les heures non travaillées (retard, mise à pied disciplinaire) n'en est pas une. Au Royaume-Uni, on parle d'« unlawful deduction from wages » ; les règles américaines varient selon les États.

def: A sanction under which the employee is sent home without pay for a few days.

formal.ex: The sanction imposed is a three-day [[disciplinary suspension without pay]].
formal.ex_us: The sanction imposed is a three-day [[unpaid disciplinary suspension]].

everyday.ex: He [[was suspended without pay]] for three days after the incident in the warehouse.

collocations: the maximum length of the suspension
note_fr: Ne traduisez jamais littéralement (« put on foot »). Il s'agit d'une sanction, dont la durée maximale doit figurer au règlement intérieur. Au Royaume-Uni, une suspension sans salaire n'est possible que si le contrat le prévoit.

explain.written: A mise à pied disciplinaire is a disciplinary sanction consisting of a short suspension of the employment contract without pay, the maximum length of which must be laid down in the company's internal rules.
explain.spoken: It's a short unpaid suspension used as a punishment - a few days at home without pay.

def: A temporary removal from the workplace while the employer decides what sanction, if any, to impose.

formal.ex: In view of the seriousness of the allegations, you are placed on [[precautionary suspension]] pending the outcome of the procedure.

everyday.ex: We [[sent him home]] while we work out what to do next.

collocations: pending the outcome of the procedure
to place someone on precautionary suspension
to confirm the suspension in writing
note_fr: Ce n'est pas une sanction mais une mesure d'attente, généralement liée à une faute grave présumée ; si la faute grave n'est finalement pas retenue, le salaire de la période est dû. Au Royaume-Uni, la « suspension » pendant l'enquête est en principe rémunérée.

explain.written: A mise à pied conservatoire is a precautionary suspension from work, with immediate effect, pending the employer's decision on a possible sanction; it is not itself a sanction.
explain.spoken: It's a holding measure: we ask the employee to stay at home until we've decided what to do. It isn't a punishment in itself.

def: To tell an employee to stay away from work for a time while a matter is looked into.

formal.us: to place on paid administrative leave
formal.ex: The employee [[was suspended on full pay]] while the matter was investigated.
formal.ex_us: The employee [[was placed on paid administrative leave]] while the matter was investigated.

everyday.ex: They've [[suspended]] two drivers until they know what happened.
everyday.ex_us: They've [[put two drivers on leave]] until they know what happened.

collocations: to keep the suspension under review
note_fr: Aux États-Unis, « administrative leave » est le terme usuel, « suspension » évoquant plutôt la sanction. Au Royaume-Uni, la suspension doit rester « a neutral act » : brève, rémunérée et sans préjuger de l'issue.

def: To end a suspension and allow the employee to return to work.

formal.ex: As the allegations have not been substantiated, [[the suspension is lifted]] with immediate effect.

everyday.ex: There's nothing in it, so let's [[bring her back]] on Monday.

collocations: with no stain on one's record
note_fr: « To lift » s'emploie pour toute mesure restrictive (a ban, a restriction, a suspension). Évitez « to raise the suspension », qui ne se dit pas.

def: A move to a lower grade or less senior job, usually with lower pay, imposed as a sanction.

formal.ex: A disciplinary [[demotion]] entails a change to the contract and therefore requires the employee's agreement.

everyday.ex: He [[was demoted]] from team leader after the audit.

informal.ex: She [[was bumped down]] a grade, which she took very badly.

collocations: to demote someone to a lower grade
demotion as an alternative to dismissal
note_fr: Contraire de « promotion ». N'employez pas « retrogradation » ni « downgrade » pour une personne (« to downgrade » s'applique à un poste ou à une note). En France, le salarié peut refuser la rétrogradation disciplinaire, l'employeur pouvant alors prononcer une autre sanction.

def: A move to another site or department imposed on an employee as a sanction.

formal.ex: The Company has decided on a [[disciplinary transfer]] to the Lille branch rather than dismissal.

everyday.ex: After the row, they [[moved him]] to another team.

collocations: to transfer someone to another site
a transfer imposed as a sanction
note_fr: « Mutation » ne s'emploie pas en anglais dans ce sens (c'est un terme de biologie). « A sideways move » désigne une mutation sans promotion ni rétrogradation.

def: A deliberate refusal to obey a reasonable instruction from a manager.

formal.uk: refusal to carry out a reasonable instruction
formal.us: refusal to carry out a reasonable instruction
formal.ex: A repeated [[refusal to carry out a reasonable instruction]] may be treated as gross misconduct.

everyday.uk: to refuse to do as one is asked
everyday.us: to refuse to do as one is asked
everyday.ex: He simply [[refuses to do as he's asked]], and the rest of the team have noticed.

informal.ex: She [[answers back]] every time her supervisor opens his mouth.
informal.ex_us: She [[talks back]] every time her supervisor opens his mouth.

note_fr: Le mot existe en anglais, mais il est plus courant dans les textes américains ; un texte britannique dira plutôt « refusal to obey a reasonable (and lawful) instruction ». Le caractère raisonnable de l'ordre est essentiel dans les trois systèmes.

def: A failure to come to work without permission or a valid reason.

formal.ex: Any [[unauthorised absence]] must be explained in writing within forty-eight hours.
formal.ex_us: Any [[unexcused absence]] must be explained in writing within forty-eight hours.

everyday.ex: He [[didn't turn up]] on Monday and didn't even ring in.
everyday.ex_us: He [[didn't show up]] on Monday and didn't even call in.

informal.ex: Our night-shift supervisor [[has gone AWOL]] again.

collocations: to ring in sick (UK) / to call in sick
note_fr: « Unjustified absence » se comprend mais sonne traduit. « AWOL » /ˈeɪwɒl/ (absent without leave) vient du vocabulaire militaire. Orthographe : « unauthorised » (UK), « unauthorized » (US).

def: Stopping coming to work, without explanation and without resigning.

formal.ex: An employee who [[abandons his or her post]] and fails to return after formal notice may be presumed to have resigned.
formal.ex_us: An employee who [[abandons his or her job]] and fails to return after formal notice may be presumed to have resigned.

everyday.ex: He [[walked out]] three weeks ago and nobody's heard from him since.

collocations: to fail to return to work
formal notice to return to work
to be treated as having resigned
note_fr: En France, depuis 2023, le salarié qui ne reprend pas son poste après mise en demeure est présumé démissionnaire. Aux États-Unis, « job abandonment » est une notion de règlement intérieur (souvent trois jours de « no-call, no-show ») assimilée à un départ volontaire. « To walk out » peut aussi signifier « débrayer ».

def: Arriving late for work again and again.

formal.ex: You have been warned on two occasions about your [[persistent lateness]].
formal.ex_us: You have been warned on two occasions about your [[repeated tardiness]].

everyday.ex: His [[poor timekeeping]] is starting to annoy the whole shift.
everyday.ex_us: His [[always being late]] is starting to annoy the whole shift.

note_fr: « Tardiness » et « tardy » sont américains ; au Royaume-Uni, on parle de « lateness » ou de « (poor) timekeeping ». « Retard » ne se traduit jamais par « retard » (terme insultant) ni par « delay » pour une personne : « he was late », pas « he had a delay ».

def: Extremely careless behaviour that shows a serious disregard for one's duties or for other people's safety.

formal.ex: Leaving the machine unguarded amounted to [[gross negligence]] and justified dismissal without notice.

everyday.ex: Nobody thinks she did it on purpose, but she [[was seriously careless]].

note_fr: Attention à la différence entre « negligent » (qui commet une négligence) et « negligible » (négligeable). La négligence, même grave, n'implique pas d'intention : c'est ce qui la distingue de « wilful misconduct ».

term.uk: breach of the duty of loyalty
term.us: breach of the duty of loyalty

def: Acting against the employer's interests while still employed, for example by working for a competitor.

formal.uk: breach of the duty of fidelity
formal.us: breach of the duty of loyalty
formal.ex: Diverting clients to a competing business while still employed is a clear [[breach of the duty of fidelity]].
formal.ex_us: Diverting clients to a competing business while still employed is a clear [[breach of the duty of loyalty]].

everyday.uk: to go behind the company's back
everyday.us: to go behind the company's back
everyday.ex: He'd been [[going behind the company's back]] for months, quoting for our own clients.

note_fr: Le droit anglais parle traditionnellement de « duty of fidelity » ; « duty of loyalty » est le terme américain et se comprend partout. « Loyal » en anglais est plus affectif que juridique : pour un écrit, préférez « in good faith ».

def: An act serious enough for the employer to be entitled to dismiss the person who commits it.

formal.ex: The policy lists examples of [[conduct warranting dismissal]] for a first offence.
formal.ex_us: The policy lists examples of [[conduct warranting termination]] for a first offense.

everyday.uk: something one can be dismissed for
everyday.us: something one can be terminated for
everyday.ex: Falsifying a timesheet is [[something you can be dismissed for]].
everyday.ex_us: Falsifying a timesheet is [[something you can be terminated for]].

informal.ex: Sleeping on the night shift is [[a sackable offence]] here.
informal.ex_us: Sleeping on the night shift is [[a fireable offense]] here.

note_fr: Orthographe : « offence » (UK), « offense » (US). « To warrant » = justifier, mériter (« the conduct warrants a final warning »). « Offence » ne signifie pas forcément infraction pénale : c'est ici le manquement disciplinaire.

def: Misconduct of the same kind committed again after an earlier warning or sanction.

formal.ex: [[Any repetition of this conduct]] will lead to further disciplinary action, which may include dismissal.

everyday.ex: If he [[does it again]], we won't be having another friendly chat.

note_fr: « Recidivism » appartient au vocabulaire pénal. Dans une lettre, la formule consacrée est « any repetition of this conduct » ou « any further misconduct ». En France, on ne peut pas sanctionner deux fois les mêmes faits, mais on peut invoquer les sanctions passées pour aggraver une faute nouvelle.

def: The things an employee is said to have done wrong, before they have been proved.

formal.ex: The letter must set out [[the allegations against the employee]] in sufficient detail for a response to be prepared.

everyday.ex: She still doesn't really know [[what she's accused of]].

collocations: to put the allegations to someone
note_fr: « The reproached facts » est un calque à proscrire, tout comme « to reproach » dans ce contexte. Tant que rien n'est établi, employez « alleged » : « the alleged theft ». « Facts » en anglais désigne ce qui est avéré.

def: A meeting held to establish what happened before deciding whether to start disciplinary proceedings.

formal.ex: You are required to attend an [[investigation meeting]], which is not a disciplinary hearing.
formal.ex_us: You are required to attend an [[investigatory interview]], which is not a disciplinary hearing.

everyday.uk: to get someone's version of events
everyday.us: to get someone's version of events
everyday.ex: Before we go any further, I'd like [[to get her version of events]].

collocations: to take a statement from a witness
note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, l'enquête (« investigation ») et l'audience disciplinaire (« hearing ») sont deux étapes distinctes, menées si possible par deux personnes différentes. Le droit français n'impose pas d'enquête formelle avant l'entretien préalable, mais l'employeur doit pouvoir prouver les faits.

def: To show, with evidence, that an allegation is true.

formal.ex: The employer was unable [[to substantiate]] the allegation of theft, and the dismissal was held to be without cause.

everyday.ex: Can we actually [[back up]] any of this, or is it just hearsay?

collocations: to have evidence to support something
note_fr: « To establish the facts » existe aussi, mais « to substantiate an allegation » est plus précis. En France, le doute profite au salarié. Au Royaume-Uni, l'employeur n'a pas à prouver la faute avec certitude : une conviction raisonnable, fondée sur une enquête sérieuse, suffit.

def: To say that one did what one is accused of.

formal.ex: During the meeting you [[admitted the allegations]] and offered no explanation.

everyday.ex: To be fair, he [[owned up to]] it straight away.

informal.ex: She finally [[came clean]] about the missing stock.

note_fr: « To recognise the facts » est un calque. Construction : « to admit (to) taking the money », jamais « to admit to have taken ». Le contraire est « to deny » (nier) ; « to contest » ou « to dispute » = contester.

def: A formal meeting at which the employer puts the allegations to the employee and hears the response before deciding on a sanction.

formal.ex: You are required to attend a [[disciplinary hearing]] on 14 March at 10 a.m.
formal.ex_us: You are required to attend a [[disciplinary meeting]] on March 14 at 10 a.m.

everyday.ex: She's got [[a disciplinary]] on Thursday and she's worried sick.
everyday.ex_us: She's got [[a disciplinary meeting]] on Thursday and she's worried sick.

note_fr: « Hearing » ne désigne pas ici une audience judiciaire : c'est une réunion interne. Aux États-Unis, aucune réunion de ce type n'est imposée par la loi dans le secteur privé non syndiqué. L'équivalent français est l'entretien préalable.

def: In French law, the compulsory meeting at which the employer explains the reasons for a proposed dismissal and listens to the employee's explanations.

formal.ex: No decision may be taken until the [[pre-dismissal meeting]] has been held.

everyday.uk: the meeting before any decision is made
everyday.us: the meeting before any decision is made
everyday.ex: Nothing is final yet; [[the meeting before any decision is made]] is there precisely so that he can explain himself.

collocations: to invite someone to a pre-dismissal meeting
to fail to attend the meeting
note_fr: « Preliminary interview » prête à confusion (« interview » évoque le recrutement). L'entretien n'est pas le lieu de la décision : la lettre ne peut partir qu'après un délai minimal de deux jours ouvrables. Insistez auprès d'un client étranger : annoncer le licenciement pendant l'entretien est une irrégularité.

explain.written: The entretien préalable is a mandatory meeting to which the employer must invite the employee before deciding on a dismissal, in order to state the reasons for the proposed measure and to hear the employee's explanations.
explain.spoken: It's a compulsory meeting before any dismissal: we tell the employee what the problem is, we listen to their side, and only afterwards do we decide.

term.uk: letter of invitation to a pre-dismissal meeting
term.us: letter of invitation to a pre-dismissal meeting

ipa.uk: /ˌletər əv ˌɪnvɪˈteɪʃ(ə)n tu ə ˌpriː dɪsˈmɪs(ə)l ˌmiːtɪŋ/
ipa.us: /ˌletər əv ˌɪnvɪˈteɪʃ(ə)n tu ə ˌpriː dɪsˈmɪs(ə)l ˌmiːtɪŋ/

def: The letter that formally invites the employee to the pre-dismissal meeting and states its purpose, date, time and place.

formal.uk: letter of invitation to a pre-dismissal meeting
formal.us: letter of invitation to a pre-dismissal meeting
formal.ex: The [[letter of invitation to a pre-dismissal meeting]] must state that a dismissal is being considered and remind the employee of the right to be assisted.

everyday.ex: The [[invitation letter]] went out on Tuesday, so the earliest we can meet is the following Wednesday.

collocations: to send out the invitation letter
to state the purpose of the meeting
at least five working days' notice
note_fr: « Convocation » en anglais désigne une cérémonie universitaire, et « to convoke » est rarissime ; « summons » est judiciaire. Dites « to invite someone to a meeting » ou, plus ferme, « to require someone to attend ». Cinq jours ouvrables au moins doivent séparer la réception de la lettre et l'entretien.

explain.written: The convocation à l'entretien préalable is the letter, sent by registered post or delivered by hand against receipt, inviting the employee to the pre-dismissal meeting and informing him or her of the right to be assisted.
explain.spoken: It's the formal letter inviting the employee to the meeting. It has to say that dismissal is on the table and that they can bring someone with them.

fr: lettre recommandée avec accusé de réception

term.us: letter sent by certified mail, return receipt requested

def: A letter sent by a postal service that provides proof of posting and of delivery.

formal.uk: by registered post with acknowledgement of receipt
formal.us: by certified mail, return receipt requested
formal.ex: Notice of dismissal shall be sent [[by registered post with acknowledgement of receipt]].
formal.ex_us: Notice of dismissal shall be sent [[by certified mail, return receipt requested]].

everyday.ex: Send it [[by recorded delivery]] so that we have proof of the date.
everyday.ex_us: Send it [[by certified mail]] so that we have proof of the date.

note_fr: « Recommended letter » est un contresens classique (« recommended » = conseillé). Au Royaume-Uni, « post » ; aux États-Unis, « mail ». En France, c'est la date de première présentation de la lettre qui fait courir la plupart des délais.

fr: remise en main propre contre décharge
def: Giving a letter to someone in person and having them sign to confirm they have received it.

formal.uk: delivered by hand against signed receipt
formal.us: delivered by hand against signed receipt
formal.ex: The invitation may be [[delivered by hand against signed receipt]] instead of being sent by post.

everyday.uk: to hand someone a letter and get them to sign for it
everyday.us: to hand someone a letter and get them to sign for it
everyday.ex: I'd [[hand him the letter and get him to sign for it]]; it saves three days.

collocations: to sign and date a copy
note_fr: « Receipt » se prononce /rɪˈsiːt/ : le p est muet. « In own hands » ne se dit pas. Signer la décharge vaut accusé de réception, non acceptation du contenu : précisez-le au salarié (« signing simply confirms that you have received the letter »).

def: To have another person with you at a formal meeting to support or advise you.

formal.ex: You are entitled [[to be accompanied by]] a colleague or a trade union representative.
formal.ex_us: You are entitled [[to be accompanied by]] a coworker or a union representative.

everyday.ex: You can [[bring someone with you]] to the meeting if you'd like.

collocations: to be assisted by a member of staff
note_fr: En France, le salarié peut être « assisté » par une personne de son choix appartenant au personnel ou, à défaut de représentants du personnel, par un conseiller du salarié. Au Royaume-Uni, le « companion » est un collègue ou un représentant syndical. Aux États-Unis, ce droit n'existe en principe que pour les salariés syndiqués (« Weingarten rights »).

def: In France, an outside volunteer, chosen from an official list, who may assist an employee at a pre-dismissal meeting in a company with no staff representatives.

formal.ex: Where the company has no staff representatives, the employee may be assisted by an [[external employee adviser]] chosen from the official list.
formal.ex_us: Where the company has no staff representatives, the employee may be assisted by an [[external employee advisor]] chosen from the official list.

everyday.ex: As there are no reps here, he's entitled to bring [[an outside adviser]] from the official list.
everyday.ex_us: As there are no reps here, he's entitled to bring [[an outside advisor]] from the official list.

collocations: to be assisted free of charge
to attend in an advisory capacity
note_fr: Ce n'est ni un avocat ni un représentant du personnel. La lettre de convocation doit indiquer où la liste peut être consultée ; l'oublier est une irrégularité de procédure. « Adviser » (UK) et « advisor » (US) sont deux orthographes admises.

explain.written: A conseiller du salarié is an external adviser, appointed by the authorities and entered on an official list, who may assist an employee free of charge at a pre-dismissal meeting where the company has no staff representatives.
explain.spoken: In a company with no employee reps, the employee can bring an outside adviser from an official list. It isn't a lawyer - more of a trained volunteer.

def: To give one's own account and explanation of what one is accused of.

formal.ex: The employee must be given a proper opportunity [[to state his or her case]] before any decision is taken.

everyday.uk: to give one's side of the story
everyday.us: to give one's side of the story
everyday.ex: The meeting is your chance [[to give your side of the story]].

collocations: to be given a fair hearing
note_fr: « To explain oneself » existe, mais il a une nuance de sommation (« Explain yourself! »). « To make representations » est la formule juridique britannique pour « présenter ses observations ».

def: A written record of what was said at a disciplinary or pre-dismissal meeting.

formal.uk: a written record of the meeting
formal.us: a written record of the meeting
formal.ex: [[A written record of the meeting]] will be sent to you for comment within five working days.

everyday.ex: Could you sit in and [[take notes]]? I'd rather not chair and write at the same time.

collocations: to sit in on a meeting
to sign the notes as agreed
note_fr: « Minutes » /ˈmɪnɪts/ convient pour une réunion collégiale ; pour un entretien individuel, on dit plutôt « notes » ou « a record ». Le droit français n'impose pas de compte rendu de l'entretien préalable ; au Royaume-Uni, c'est une bonne pratique constante.

def: To stop a meeting or hearing for a time, intending to continue it later.

formal.ex: The chair [[adjourned the hearing]] to allow the new evidence to be examined.

everyday.ex: Shall we [[take a break]] for ten minutes and then carry on?

collocations: to adjourn to consider the decision
note_fr: Le d de « adjourn » est muet : /əˈdʒɜːn/. « To adjourn » = interrompre une réunion commencée ; « to postpone » = reporter une réunion qui n'a pas encore eu lieu. « To reconvene » = reprendre la séance.

def: The period after which an employer who knew of an act of misconduct can no longer start proceedings about it.

formal.ex: As the employer had known of the facts for more than two months, any disciplinary action [[was time-barred]].

everyday.ex: If HR knew back in January, I'm afraid we[['re out of time]].

collocations: within two months of becoming aware of the facts
to run from the date of knowledge
note_fr: « Prescription » en anglais est une ordonnance médicale. Pour un délai de prescription, dites « time limit » ou « limitation period ». En France, l'employeur dispose de deux mois à compter du jour où il a connaissance des faits ; le Royaume-Uni n'a pas de délai chiffré, mais exige d'agir « without unreasonable delay ».

def: The principle that an employee cannot be disciplined a second time for misconduct that has already been sanctioned.

formal.uk: to be sanctioned twice for the same conduct
formal.us: to be sanctioned twice for the same conduct
formal.ex: No employee may [[be sanctioned twice for the same conduct]].

everyday.uk: to punish someone twice for the same thing
everyday.us: to punish someone twice for the same thing
everyday.ex: We've already given him a warning for that, and we can't [[punish him twice for the same thing]].

informal.ex: Dismissing her now for the March incident would be [[double jeopardy]].

note_fr: « Double jeopardy » est à l'origine un terme pénal ; son emploi en RH est imagé. Piège pratique à signaler à un client : en France, un courriel de reproches peut être requalifié en avertissement et « épuiser » le pouvoir disciplinaire pour les faits qu'il vise.

def: A sanction whose severity matches the seriousness of the misconduct.

formal.ex: The sanction must be [[proportionate to]] the seriousness of the misconduct.

everyday.ex: Dismissal for one late report would look [[heavy-handed]].

informal.ex: A final warning for that? It's a bit [[over the top]].

collocations: to err on the side of leniency
note_fr: « Proportionate » (adapté à la gravité) et non « proportional » (mathématique). « Heavy-handed » = qui a la main lourde. En France, le juge peut annuler une sanction disproportionnée autre que le licenciement.

def: Facts that do not excuse misconduct but make it less serious, such as long service or personal difficulties.

formal.ex: In deciding on the sanction, the Company has taken into account the [[mitigating circumstances]] you put forward.

everyday.ex: We should [[make allowances for]] what he was going through at home.

note_fr: « Attenuating circumstances » existe mais reste rare. Ne confondez pas « to mitigate » (atténuer) et « to militate against » (jouer contre). Le contraire : « aggravating factors ».

def: The fact of never having received a disciplinary sanction.

formal.ex: The tribunal noted the employee's [[unblemished record]] over nineteen years' service.

everyday.ex: She's got a [[clean record]], which makes dismissal for a first offence hard to justify.

note_fr: « Virgin file » fait sourire. Le nom « record » se prononce /ˈrekɔːd/ (accent sur la première syllabe), le verbe /rɪˈkɔːd/. « Track record » désigne les résultats passés, pas le passé disciplinaire.

def: The decision reached at the end of a disciplinary procedure.

formal.uk: to notify someone of the outcome
formal.us: to notify someone of the outcome
formal.ex: You will [[be notified of the outcome]] in writing within five working days of the hearing.

everyday.uk: to let someone know what has been decided
everyday.us: to let someone know what has been decided
everyday.ex: We'll [[let you know what's been decided]] by the end of the week.

note_fr: « Issue » est un faux ami : « an issue » = un problème, une question. Pour « l'issue », dites « outcome ». « To notify » est transitif direct de la personne : « to notify the employee of the decision », non « to notify the decision to the employee ».

def: The letter by which the employer informs the employee of the dismissal and of the reasons for it.

formal.ex: The [[letter of dismissal]] must set out the reasons relied on by the employer.
formal.ex_us: The [[letter of termination]] must set out the reasons relied on by the employer.

everyday.ex: Could you look over the [[dismissal letter]] before it goes out?
everyday.ex_us: Could you look over the [[termination letter]] before it goes out?

collocations: the date the letter was sent
note_fr: « Licence letter » ou « licensing letter » n'ont aucun rapport (« licence » = autorisation, permis). En France, la lettre doit être motivée et ne peut être expédiée moins de deux jours ouvrables après l'entretien. Aux États-Unis, aucun écrit motivé n'est en principe exigé.

def: The reason that legally justifies ending someone's employment.

formal.ex: Repeated unauthorised absence constitutes [[grounds for dismissal]].
formal.ex_us: Repeated unexcused absence constitutes [[grounds for termination]].

everyday.ex: What exactly is our [[reason for dismissing him]]?
everyday.ex_us: What exactly is our [[reason for terminating him]]?

note_fr: « Motive » désigne le mobile (d'un crime) : ne l'employez pas pour « motif ». « Grounds » est presque toujours au pluriel ; « on the grounds that... » introduit une proposition, « on grounds of... » un nom.

fr: la lettre de licenciement fixe les limites du litige

term.uk: to define the scope of the dispute
term.us: to define the scope of the dispute

def: The French rule that an employer who is sued can rely only on the reasons given in the dismissal letter.

formal.uk: to define the scope of the dispute
formal.us: to define the scope of the dispute
formal.ex: The reasons stated in the dismissal letter [[define the scope of the dispute]]: no other ground may subsequently be relied on.

everyday.uk: to be stuck with what the letter says
everyday.us: to be stuck with what the letter says
everyday.ex: Once it has gone out, we [[are stuck with what the letter says]], so let's get it right.

collocations: to clarify the reasons after the event
note_fr: Point capital pour un client anglo-saxon : en France, un motif absent de la lettre ne peut pas être invoqué devant le juge. L'employeur peut seulement préciser les motifs énoncés, dans un bref délai après la notification, non en ajouter. « To rely on » = invoquer, se prévaloir de.

explain.written: Under French law the dismissal letter defines the scope of the dispute: before the court, the employer may rely only on the reasons stated in that letter.
explain.spoken: Whatever we put in the letter is what we'll have to defend in court - we can't come up with new reasons later.

def: In French law, the valid reason every dismissal requires: one based on true, verifiable facts that are serious enough to justify ending the contract.

formal.ex: A dismissal that is not based on a [[real and serious cause]] entitles the employee to damages.

everyday.ex: In France you need [[a genuine and serious reason]] to dismiss anyone, and you have to be able to prove it.

collocations: to be based on a real and serious cause
dismissal without real and serious cause
note_fr: Traduction consacrée, à faire suivre du terme français à la première occurrence. L'équivalent fonctionnel britannique est le « fair reason » ; aux États-Unis, « just cause » n'existe que dans les contrats et conventions collectives, l'emploi « at-will » ne requérant aucun motif.

explain.written: Under French law, any dismissal must be based on a real and serious cause (cause réelle et sérieuse), that is, on objective, verifiable facts of sufficient gravity to justify termination of the contract.
explain.spoken: You always need a genuine reason, backed by facts you can prove, and serious enough to justify ending the contract.

def: In French law, any dismissal based on a reason relating to the individual employee (conduct, performance, unfitness), as opposed to an economic reason.

formal.uk: dismissal for a reason relating to the employee personally
formal.us: termination for a reason relating to the employee personally
formal.ex: A [[dismissal for a reason relating to the employee personally]] may be disciplinary or non-disciplinary.
formal.ex_us: A [[termination for a reason relating to the employee personally]] may be disciplinary or non-disciplinary.

everyday.uk: a dismissal that's about the individual
everyday.us: a termination that's about the individual
everyday.ex: This is [[a dismissal that's about the individual]], not about the job, so the economic rules don't apply.
everyday.ex_us: This is [[a termination that's about the individual]], not about the job, so the economic rules don't apply.

collocations: as opposed to dismissal on economic grounds
a reason inherent in the person
note_fr: Attention : « personal reasons » évoque en anglais des raisons privées (« he left for personal reasons »). Précisez toujours : « a reason relating to the employee, such as conduct or performance ». Le droit britannique classe plutôt par « conduct », « capability » et « redundancy ».

explain.written: French law distinguishes dismissal for personal reasons (licenciement pour motif personnel), which is based on the employee's conduct, performance or fitness, from dismissal on economic grounds, which is unrelated to the individual.
explain.spoken: French law has two families of dismissal: one where the reason is the person - conduct or performance - and one where the reason is economic.

def: A dismissal decided as a sanction for something the employee did wrong.

formal.ex: A [[dismissal on disciplinary grounds]] must be notified within one month of the meeting.
formal.ex_us: A [[termination on disciplinary grounds]] must be notified within one month of the meeting.

everyday.ex: He [[was dismissed for misconduct]], not for poor performance, and the two procedures are different.
everyday.ex_us: He [[was terminated for misconduct]], not for poor performance, and the two procedures are different.

collocations: to treat a matter as disciplinary
note_fr: Distinction essentielle en France : l'insuffisance professionnelle n'est pas une faute. Se placer à tort sur le terrain disciplinaire prive le licenciement de cause réelle et sérieuse. Le Royaume-Uni distingue de même « conduct » et « capability ».

term.uk: to notify someone of their dismissal
term.us: to notify someone of their termination

def: To inform an employee officially that they are being dismissed.

formal.uk: to give written notice of dismissal
formal.us: to give written notice of termination
formal.ex: The employer must [[give written notice of dismissal]] by registered post.
formal.ex_us: The employer must [[give written notice of termination]] by certified mail.

everyday.uk: to tell someone they are being let go
everyday.us: to tell someone they are being let go
everyday.ex: Who's going [[to tell her she's being let go]]?

informal.uk: to give someone the bad news
informal.us: to give someone the bad news
informal.ex: I'd rather [[give him the bad news]] myself than let him hear it from the team.

collocations: to confirm the dismissal in writing
to break the news to someone
note_fr: Construction : « to notify someone of something ». En France, la notification se fait obligatoirement par lettre recommandée, jamais oralement : un licenciement annoncé de vive voix avant l'envoi de la lettre est sans cause réelle et sérieuse.

def: Dismissal that takes effect at once, without any notice period, because of very serious misconduct.

formal.ex: Gross misconduct will normally result in [[summary dismissal]].
formal.ex_us: Gross misconduct will normally result in [[immediate termination]].

everyday.ex: She [[was dismissed without notice]] after the cash went missing.
everyday.ex_us: She [[was terminated without notice]] after the cash went missing.

informal.uk: to be sacked on the spot
informal.us: to be fired on the spot
informal.ex: He [[was sacked on the spot]] for hitting a colleague.
informal.ex_us: He [[was fired on the spot]] for hitting a coworker.

collocations: without notice or payment in lieu
note_fr: « Summary » signifie ici « sans préavis », non « sans procédure » : même pour une faute grave, il faut un entretien préalable en France et une audience disciplinaire au Royaume-Uni. « Summarily » se prononce /ˈsʌmərəli/.

def: Starting now, without any delay or notice.

formal.ex: Your employment is terminated [[with immediate effect]].
formal.ex_us: Your employment is terminated [[effective immediately]].

everyday.ex: [[As of today]], he's no longer on the payroll.

informal.ex: They took his badge off him [[there and then]].
informal.ex_us: They took his badge from him [[then and there]].

collocations: to take effect on receipt of this letter
from the date of this letter
note_fr: « Immediately effective » ne se dit pas. Notez l'inversion des deux formules : « with immediate effect » (UK) et « effective immediately » (US). « With effect from » + date est la tournure standard pour une prise d'effet différée.

def: To lose a right or a payment as a consequence of one's own conduct.

formal.ex: An employee dismissed for gross misconduct [[forfeits]] both notice and statutory severance pay.

everyday.ex: If it's gross misconduct, he [[loses out on]] his severance.

note_fr: « Forfeit » se prononce /ˈfɔːfɪt/ (comme « fit ») et n'a aucun rapport avec « forfait » (« flat rate », « package »). En France, même en cas de faute grave ou lourde, l'indemnité compensatrice de congés payés reste due.

def: A dismissal that the law treats as unjustified or improperly carried out, giving the employee a claim against the employer.

formal.ex: The claimant brought a complaint of [[unfair dismissal]] before the employment tribunal.
formal.ex_us: The plaintiff filed a [[wrongful termination]] suit in state court.

everyday.ex: She's convinced she [[was unfairly dismissed]], and she may well have a point.
everyday.ex_us: She's convinced she [[was wrongfully terminated]], and she may well have a point.

collocations: dismissal without real and serious cause (France)
note_fr: Trois notions à ne pas confondre. France : licenciement sans cause réelle et sérieuse. Royaume-Uni : « unfair dismissal », droit légal soumis à une condition d'ancienneté. États-Unis : « wrongful termination », limité aux cas où la rupture viole la loi, l'ordre public ou un contrat. « Abusive dismissal » est un calque.

fr: licenciement en violation du contrat (« wrongful dismissal »)
def: In English law, a dismissal in breach of the contract of employment, typically without the notice the contract requires.

formal.ex: Having been dismissed without notice in the absence of gross misconduct, he succeeded in his claim for [[wrongful dismissal]].

everyday.uk: to be dismissed in breach of contract
everyday.us: to be dismissed in breach of contract
everyday.ex: Strictly speaking, she [[was dismissed in breach of contract]], because they never paid her notice.

note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, « wrongful » (contraire au contrat : préavis non respecté) et « unfair » (contraire à la loi : absence de motif ou de procédure équitable) sont deux actions distinctes et cumulables. Aux États-Unis, « wrongful termination » ou « wrongful discharge » a un sens plus large.

def: In UK law, one of the categories of reason (conduct, capability, redundancy, a legal bar, or some other substantial reason) that can justify a dismissal.

formal.ex: The employer must first show that the dismissal was for a [[potentially fair reason]], such as conduct or capability.

everyday.ex: Do we have [[a fair reason]], and can we show we went about it properly?

collocations: to act reasonably in all the circumstances
the reason shown by the employer
note_fr: Notion britannique sans équivalent américain. « Potentially » : avoir un motif légitime ne suffit pas, l'employeur doit en outre avoir agi raisonnablement et suivi une procédure équitable. Rapprochez-la de la cause réelle et sérieuse sans les assimiler.

fr: marge d'appréciation de l'employeur raisonnable (droit britannique)
def: The UK test under which a dismissal is fair if a reasonable employer could have decided to dismiss in the same circumstances.

formal.uk: to fall within the band of reasonable responses
formal.us: to fall within the band of reasonable responses
formal.ex: The tribunal found that dismissal [[fell within the band of reasonable responses]] open to the employer.

everyday.uk: something a reasonable employer might have done
everyday.us: something a reasonable employer might have done
everyday.ex: The question isn't whether we'd have sacked him ourselves, but whether it's [[something a reasonable employer might have done]].

collocations: outside the range of reasonable responses
note_fr: Le juge britannique ne substitue pas sa propre appréciation à celle de l'employeur ; le juge français, lui, contrôle directement le caractère réel et sérieux du motif. Utile pour expliquer à un client britannique pourquoi le contrôle français lui paraît plus strict.

def: To carry out each step that the law or the company's rules require before dismissing or disciplining someone.

formal.ex: Even where the reason is sound, the employer must [[follow a fair procedure]].
formal.ex_us: Even where the reason is sound, the employer must [[follow the proper procedure]].

everyday.ex: It'll take three weeks longer, but we need [[to do things properly]].

informal.uk: to do it by the book
informal.us: to do it by the book
informal.ex: With his lawyer watching every step, we have [[to do it by the book]].

note_fr: « To respect the procedure » est un calque : on « follows » ou on « complies with » une procédure. « Due process » se dit surtout aux États-Unis. « To cut corners » = brûler les étapes.

def: A failure to follow one of the required steps of a procedure correctly.

formal.ex: A [[procedural irregularity]] does not in itself deprive the dismissal of real and serious cause, but it does give rise to compensation.

everyday.ex: One [[slip in the procedure]] and we hand his lawyer an easy argument.

collocations: to cure a defect on appeal
note_fr: En France, on distingue l'irrégularité de procédure (indemnité limitée) de l'absence de cause réelle et sérieuse. Au Royaume-Uni, un vice de procédure peut à lui seul rendre le licenciement « unfair ». « A technicality » = un point de pure forme.

def: A false reason given to hide the real reason for a dismissal.

formal.ex: The court found that the alleged restructuring was a mere [[pretext]] for removing an employee who had complained.

everyday.ex: Everyone could see the reorganisation was just [[an excuse]] to get rid of her.
everyday.ex_us: Everyone could see the reorganization was just [[an excuse]] to get rid of her.

informal.ex: They sacked him for some [[trumped-up reason]] about his expenses.
informal.ex_us: They fired him for some [[trumped-up reason]] about his expenses.

collocations: the real reason for the dismissal
note_fr: Aux États-Unis, « pretext » est un terme technique du contentieux de la discrimination : le salarié cherche à montrer que le motif invoqué est « pretextual ». « Sham » = fictif, de façade.

def: In French law, a dismissal treated as never having taken place because it breaches a fundamental right or a statutory protection.

formal.ex: A dismissal on a discriminatory ground is [[null and void]], and the employee may ask to return to his or her job.

everyday.ex: If the judge decides she was dismissed because she was pregnant, the dismissal [[won't stand]].

collocations: to be entitled to return to one's job
note_fr: À distinguer du licenciement sans cause réelle et sérieuse : la nullité vise les cas les plus graves (discrimination, harcèlement, maternité, atteinte à une liberté fondamentale, salarié protégé licencié sans autorisation). L'analogue britannique le plus proche est l'« automatically unfair dismissal ».

explain.written: A dismissal is void (licenciement nul) under French law where it infringes a fundamental freedom or a specific statutory protection; the employee may then seek either a return to the job or enhanced compensation.
explain.spoken: In the worst cases, such as discrimination, the dismissal is simply cancelled: legally, it's as if it never happened.

def: In France, an employee, typically a staff or union representative, who cannot be dismissed without prior authorisation from the labour inspector.

formal.ex: The dismissal of a [[protected employee]] is subject to the prior authorisation of the labour inspector.
formal.ex_us: The dismissal of a [[protected employee]] is subject to the prior authorization of the labor inspector.

everyday.ex: He sits on the works council, so he [[has protected status]] and we can't move without the labour inspector.
everyday.ex_us: He sits on the works council, so he [[has protected status]] and we can't move without the labor inspector.

collocations: to seek authorisation from the labour inspector
note_fr: Ne confondez pas avec « protected class » ou « protected characteristic », qui relèvent du droit de la discrimination. Ni le Royaume-Uni ni les États-Unis n'exigent d'autorisation administrative préalable au licenciement d'un représentant du personnel.

explain.written: A salarié protégé is an employee, in particular a staff or trade union representative, whose dismissal requires the prior authorisation of the labour inspectorate, failing which it is void.
explain.spoken: Employee reps have special protection in France: you can't dismiss them without the labour inspector's green light first.

def: A failure to do one's job to the standard the employer can reasonably expect, without any deliberate wrongdoing.

formal.ex: The dismissal is based on [[unsatisfactory performance]], evidenced by the facts set out below.

everyday.ex: We've been living with his [[underperformance]] for a year; it's time to deal with it.

informal.uk: not to be up to the job
informal.us: not to be up to the job
informal.ex: Between ourselves, she's just [[not up to the job]].

note_fr: « Professional insufficiency » ne veut rien dire en anglais. « Performance » est ici indénombrable. En France, l'insuffisance professionnelle n'est pas fautive : le licenciement est non disciplinaire et doit reposer sur des faits précis, l'employeur ayant fourni moyens et formation.

def: To fail to reach the results one was asked to achieve.

formal.uk: to fail to meet one's objectives
formal.us: to fail to meet one's objectives
formal.ex: You [[have failed to meet your objectives]] for three consecutive quarters.

everyday.ex: He's [[missed his targets]] three quarters in a row.
everyday.ex_us: He's [[missed his numbers]] three quarters in a row.

note_fr: On « meets », « hits » ou « reaches » un objectif ; on ne l'« attains » guère et on ne le « realises » pas. En France, l'insuffisance de résultats ne justifie un licenciement que si les objectifs étaient réalistes et si l'échec est imputable au salarié.

def: To tell someone formally or informally that there is a problem that needs attention.

formal.ex: Your manager [[raised concerns]] about the quality of your reports on three occasions.

everyday.ex: I [[flagged]] it with him back in the spring, so it won't come as a surprise.

collocations: to raise a concern with someone
to bring something to someone's attention
note_fr: « To raise » (transitif : soulever) et non « to rise » (intransitif : monter). « To flag something (up) » = signaler. Préférez « concerns » à « problems » : plus diplomatique, et tout aussi clair.

fr: ne pas être à la hauteur des attentes
def: To be less good than was expected or required.

formal.uk: to fall short of the required standard
formal.us: to fall short of the required standard
formal.ex: Your work continues [[to fall short of the required standard]] despite the support provided.

everyday.uk: not to be up to scratch
everyday.us: not to be up to par
everyday.ex: His last two reports [[weren't up to scratch]].
everyday.ex_us: His last two reports [[weren't up to par]].

informal.ex: I like him, but he's just [[not cutting it]] in a client-facing role.

collocations: a gap between expected and actual performance
note_fr: « Not up to scratch » est britannique, « not up to par » plutôt américain. « To be at the height » est un calque. « He's not cutting it » est familier : à réserver aux échanges entre collègues, jamais devant l'intéressé.

def: The specific aspects of someone's work that need to get better.

formal.ex: The plan identifies three [[areas requiring improvement]] and the standard expected in each.

everyday.ex: We agreed on three [[things to work on]] before the next review.

note_fr: « Axes of improvement » est un calque très répandu chez les francophones. « Shortcomings » = lacunes, plus direct ; « development areas » est l'euphémisme RH. « Weaknesses » peut blesser dans un écrit remis au salarié.

def: A written plan that sets out what an underperforming employee must improve, by when, and with what support.

formal.ex: You will be placed on a [[performance improvement plan]] for a period of three months.

everyday.ex: She's been on a [[PIP]] since January and the numbers are finally moving.

collocations: to put someone on a PIP
note_fr: « PIP » se prononce comme un mot : /pɪp/. Courant au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, le dispositif n'a pas de statut légal en France, où il sert surtout à prouver que le salarié a été alerté et accompagné. Mal conduit, il peut être perçu comme une sanction déguisée ou une mise sous pression.

def: A meeting held at regular intervals to look at the progress made since the last one.

formal.ex: A [[review meeting]] will be held every fortnight for the duration of the plan.
formal.ex_us: A [[review meeting]] will be held every two weeks for the duration of the plan.

everyday.ex: Let's have a quick [[catch-up]] every other Friday to see how it's going.
everyday.ex_us: Let's have a quick [[check-in]] every other Friday to see how it's going.

collocations: at the end of the review period
note_fr: « Point » ne se traduit pas : « to make a point » = faire valoir un argument. Dites « to have a catch-up », « to touch base » ou « to review progress ». « Fortnight » (quinze jours) est britannique et inconnu de la plupart des Américains.

fr: laisser une chance réelle de s'améliorer

term.uk: to give someone a reasonable opportunity to improve
term.us: to give someone a reasonable opportunity to improve

ipa.uk: /ˌɡɪv ˌsʌmwʌn ə ˌriːz(ə)nəb(ə)l ˌɒpəˌtjuːnəti tu ɪmˈpruːv/
ipa.us: /ˌɡɪv ˌsʌmwʌn ə ˌriːz(ə)nəb(ə)l ˌɑːpərˌtuːnəti tu ɪmˈpruːv/

def: To allow an underperforming employee enough time and support to reach the required standard before any decision is taken.

formal.ex: The employee must be given [[a reasonable opportunity to improve]], together with appropriate training and support.

everyday.ex: Three weeks isn't [[a fair chance]]; let's give her three months and some proper coaching.

note_fr: « Opportunity » et non « occasion » (qui désigne un événement). « To turn things around » = redresser la situation. Dans les trois pays, c'est ce point que le juge ou l'avocat adverse examinera en premier : délai, moyens, formation.

def: To give an employee on an improvement plan more time before a final assessment is made.

formal.ex: In view of the progress made, the Company has decided [[to extend the review period]] by six weeks.

everyday.ex: He's nearly there, so I'd [[give it another month]].

collocations: to reassess at the end of the period
to bring the plan to a close
note_fr: « To prolong » existe mais s'emploie surtout pour ce qui dure trop (« to prolong the agony ») ; pour un délai, on dit « to extend ». De même « an extension », non « a prolongation ».

def: Progress that is maintained over time and does not slip back once the pressure is off.

formal.ex: Failure to achieve a [[sustained improvement]] may lead to further action, including dismissal.

everyday.ex: The last two months have been good; the question is whether he can [[keep it up]].

collocations: to achieve and maintain the required standard
note_fr: « Sustained » (qui se maintient) n'est pas « sustainable » (durable au sens écologique ou économique). « To slip back » = retomber dans ses travers. « A marked improvement » = une nette amélioration.

def: The formal process an employer follows when an employee cannot do the job to the required standard, as opposed to refusing to.

formal.ex: Matters of poor performance are dealt with under the [[capability procedure]], not the disciplinary procedure.
formal.ex_us: Matters of poor performance are dealt with under the [[performance management process]], not the disciplinary procedure.

everyday.ex: We've been [[performance-managing]] him since the autumn.
everyday.ex_us: We've been [[performance-managing]] him since the fall.

note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, « capability » recouvre l'insuffisance professionnelle et l'inaptitude pour raison de santé. La distinction « can't / won't » (ne peut pas / ne veut pas) recoupe la distinction française entre insuffisance professionnelle et faute.

fr: constituer un dossier / garder des traces écrites
def: To keep written records of events so that they can be proved later.

formal.uk: to keep a written record of
formal.us: to keep a written record of
formal.ex: Managers are required [[to keep a written record of]] every performance discussion.

everyday.ex: If it isn't [[documented]], it didn't happen.

informal.ex: Follow up every conversation with an email so that you [[leave a paper trail]].

note_fr: « To constitute a file » est un calque. « To build a case against someone » se dit, mais suggère une intention de nuire : devant un client, parlez plutôt de « documenting the issues ». « Contemporaneous notes » = notes prises sur le moment.

fr: fixer des objectifs inatteignables (pour justifier un départ)

term.uk: to set someone up to fail
term.us: to set someone up to fail

def: To put someone in a situation, for instance by setting impossible targets, in which they cannot succeed.

formal.ex: A plan that [[sets unattainable objectives]] cannot be relied on as evidence of poor performance.

everyday.uk: to set someone up to fail
everyday.us: to set someone up to fail
everyday.ex: Doubling her target in the middle of a PIP looks like we're [[setting her up to fail]].

informal.ex: Every time he gets close, his manager [[moves the goalposts]].

note_fr: « To move the goalposts » = changer les règles en cours de route. « A foregone conclusion » = une issue jouée d'avance. Un PIP perçu comme une formalité préalable au licenciement fragilise le dossier, en France comme ailleurs.

def: To use performance procedures or pressure with the real aim of getting an employee to leave.

formal.ex: The claimant alleged that the plan had been used [[to engineer her departure]].

everyday.ex: Be honest with me: are we trying to help him improve or [[to manage him out]]?

informal.ex: They [[eased him out]] after the merger.
informal.ex_us: They [[pushed him out]] after the merger.

collocations: to be managed out of the business
to see the writing on the wall
note_fr: Jargon RH que l'on entend en réunion mais que l'on n'écrit jamais : dans un courriel, la formule peut devenir une pièce à charge. « To see the writing on the wall » = comprendre que la fin est proche.

def: The loss of a job because the employer no longer needs the position, not because of anything the employee has done.

formal.us: termination as part of a layoff
formal.ex: The [[dismissal by reason of redundancy]] of an employee presupposes that the job itself has ceased to exist.
formal.ex_us: The [[termination as part of a layoff]] of an employee presupposes that the job itself has ceased to exist.

everyday.ex: There were forty [[redundancies]] at the Leeds site last year.
everyday.ex_us: There were forty [[layoffs]] at the Ohio plant last year.

note_fr: « Economic dismissal » se comprend mais n'est pas idiomatique ; pour le droit français, écrivez « dismissal on economic grounds ». Au Royaume-Uni, « lay-off » désigne une mise en chômage technique temporaire, non un licenciement : gare au malentendu transatlantique.

def: To end someone's employment because their job is no longer needed.

formal.uk: to dismiss by reason of redundancy
formal.ex: Twelve employees will [[be dismissed by reason of redundancy]] at the end of the quarter.
formal.ex_us: Twelve employees will [[be laid off]] at the end of the quarter.

everyday.ex: They [[made her redundant]] when the Paris office closed.
everyday.ex_us: They [[laid her off]] when the Paris office closed.

note_fr: Attention à la construction : « she was made redundant », jamais « she was redundanced » ni « she was fired » (qui suppose une faute). « Laid off » : participe irrégulier de « to lay ».

def: In French law, the reasons unrelated to the individual employee (such as economic difficulties or technological change) that can justify a dismissal.

formal.ex: A dismissal [[on economic grounds]] is one made for reasons unrelated to the employee personally, resulting from the elimination or transformation of the job.

everyday.ex: It has nothing to do with her work; the job is going [[for business reasons]].

collocations: a reorganisation needed to safeguard competitiveness
note_fr: « Economic » (relatif à l'économie) et non « economical » (économe, peu coûteux). Le droit français énumère des causes précises et contrôle leur réalité ; aux États-Unis, la décision relève du « business judgment » de l'employeur et n'a pas à être justifiée.

def: In French law, the dismissal of a single employee for an economic reason, which follows its own procedure, distinct from collective dismissals.

formal.ex: An [[individual dismissal on economic grounds]] requires a pre-dismissal meeting and a prior search for an alternative position.

everyday.ex: It's [[a single redundancy]], so the procedure is fairly light, but it's still a procedure.
everyday.ex_us: It's [[a one-off layoff]], so the procedure is fairly light, but it's still a procedure.

collocations: to look for an alternative position first
as opposed to a collective procedure
note_fr: Même pour un seul poste, l'employeur français doit justifier du motif économique, rechercher un reclassement et tenir un entretien préalable. Les licenciements collectifs obéissent à des règles propres, traitées dans un autre thème.

explain.written: An individual dismissal on economic grounds (licenciement économique individuel) is the dismissal of one employee for a reason unrelated to him or her personally; it is subject to a specific procedure including a pre-dismissal meeting.
explain.spoken: Even if you're cutting just one job for economic reasons, there's a set procedure - a meeting, a letter, and a search for another role first.

def: The removal of a number of jobs from an organisation.

formal.ex: The plan provides for [[the elimination of positions]] in the finance department.

everyday.ex: The [[job cuts]] were announced on Monday morning.

informal.ex: The group is [[axing jobs]] across Europe.

note_fr: « Suppression » en anglais signifie répression ou dissimulation (« suppression of evidence ») : ne dites pas « job suppression ». « To axe » appartient au style journalistique. En droit français, c'est le poste qui est supprimé, non la personne.

def: A significant change to the way a company or department is organised, often involving job losses.

formal.ex: The proposed [[restructuring]] will result in the closure of two regional offices.

everyday.ex: After the [[reorganisation]], her role simply disappeared.
everyday.ex_us: After the [[reorganization]], her role simply disappeared.

informal.ex: There's a big [[shake-up]] coming in the sales team.

note_fr: « Restructuration » n'existe pas : le nom est « restructuring ». « To rationalise » et « to streamline » sont des euphémismes fréquents ; « downsizing » et « rightsizing » appartiennent au jargon managérial américain.

def: The minimum sum the law requires an employer to pay an employee who is dismissed, calculated on length of service.

formal.ex: Employees with the required length of service are entitled to [[statutory severance pay]], save in the event of gross misconduct.

everyday.ex: How much [[severance]] would she get after twelve years?

collocations: to be entitled to severance pay
note_fr: « Indemnity » ne convient pas (c'est une garantie contre un préjudice). Au Royaume-Uni, la seule indemnité légale est le « statutory redundancy pay », réservé au licenciement économique. Aux États-Unis, le droit fédéral n'impose aucune « severance » : elle est contractuelle ou négociée. En France, elle est due au-delà d'une ancienneté minimale, sauf faute grave ou lourde.

term.uk: severance pay under the collective agreement
term.us: severance pay under the collective agreement

def: In France, the severance pay laid down by the applicable collective agreement, which replaces the statutory amount whenever it is higher.

formal.uk: severance pay provided for by the collective agreement
formal.us: severance pay provided for by the collective agreement
formal.ex: The employee is entitled to the [[severance pay provided for by the collective agreement]] where it is more favourable than the statutory amount.
formal.ex_us: The employee is entitled to the [[severance pay provided for by the collective agreement]] where it is more favorable than the statutory amount.

everyday.uk: the enhanced rate under the collective agreement
everyday.us: the enhanced rate under the collective agreement
everyday.ex: Check the sector agreement: [[the enhanced rate under the collective agreement]] is often well above the legal minimum.

collocations: more favourable than the statutory minimum
note_fr: « Conventional » signifie « classique, traditionnel » : « conventional severance » est un contresens. Les deux indemnités ne se cumulent pas : seule la plus favorable est versée. « Enhanced » = supérieur au minimum légal.

explain.written: The indemnité conventionnelle de licenciement is the severance pay fixed by the applicable collective agreement; it is paid in place of the statutory severance pay whenever it is more favourable to the employee.
explain.spoken: Most sector agreements set their own severance scale. The employee gets whichever is higher - the legal minimum or the agreement's figure.

term.uk: pay in lieu of untaken holiday

def: The sum paid at the end of the contract for leave the employee has earned but not taken.

formal.uk: payment in lieu of accrued but untaken holiday
formal.us: payment for accrued but unused vacation
formal.ex: Your final salary will include a [[payment in lieu of accrued but untaken holiday]].
formal.ex_us: Your final paycheck will include a [[payment for accrued but unused vacation]].

everyday.uk: to be paid for the holiday one hasn't taken
everyday.us: to be paid out for unused vacation
everyday.ex: You'll [[be paid for the holiday you haven't taken]], whatever the reason for leaving.
everyday.ex_us: You'll [[be paid out for unused vacation]], whatever the reason for leaving.

note_fr: « In lieu » se prononce /ɪn ˈljuː/ ou /ɪn ˈluː/. « To accrue » = acquérir progressivement. En France, cette indemnité est due quel que soit le motif de la rupture, faute lourde comprise. Aux États-Unis, tout dépend de l'État et de la politique de l'entreprise.

def: All the sums still owed to an employee when the contract ends, and, in France, the document listing them that the employee is asked to sign.

formal.ex: On your last day you will be asked to sign a [[receipt for final payment]] listing the sums paid to you.

everyday.ex: Your [[final pay]] will go through with the March payroll.
everyday.ex_us: Your [[final paycheck]] will go out with the March payroll.

collocations: to settle up with an employee
to sign for one's final pay
note_fr: N'employez pas « settlement » seul, qui évoque une transaction. En France, le reçu pour solde de tout compte peut être dénoncé par le salarié dans un délai limité après sa signature ; le signer ne vaut donc pas renonciation à agir. Rien de tel au Royaume-Uni ni aux États-Unis.

explain.written: The solde de tout compte is the statement of all sums paid to the employee on termination; the employee signs a receipt for it, which he or she may nonetheless challenge within a limited period.
explain.spoken: It's the final pay statement: everything we owe on the last day, listed on one document that the employee signs to say they've received it.

def: The documents an employer must give an employee when the contract ends.

formal.ex: The [[end-of-contract documents]], including the certificate of employment, will be made available to you on your last day.

everyday.ex: Payroll will send your [[leaving paperwork]] by the end of the month.
everyday.ex_us: Payroll will send your [[separation paperwork]] by the end of the month.

collocations: to issue the documents without delay
note_fr: En France : certificat de travail, attestation destinée à l'assurance chômage et reçu pour solde de tout compte. Au Royaume-Uni, le document clé est le « P45 » ; aux États-Unis, il n'existe pas de liste fédérale uniforme. « Certificate of employment » n'est pas une lettre de recommandation (« reference »).

explain.written: On termination, a French employer must provide a set of end-of-contract documents: a certificate of employment, a certificate for the unemployment insurance body and a receipt for final payment.
explain.spoken: When someone leaves, we have to hand over three documents: a work certificate, a form for the unemployment office and the final pay statement.

def: To give back everything that belongs to the employer when one leaves.

formal.ex: You are required [[to return all company property]], including your laptop, access badge and any documents, by your last working day.

everyday.ex: Don't forget [[to hand back]] your laptop and your pass.
everyday.ex_us: Don't forget [[to turn in]] your laptop and your badge.

note_fr: « Material » = matière, matériau ; pour le matériel, dites « equipment » ou « property ». « To give back » est correct mais familier ; « to restitute » n'existe pas dans cet emploi. « To clear one's desk » = vider son bureau.

term.uk: to escort someone off the premises
term.us: to escort someone off the premises

def: To accompany a dismissed or suspended employee out of the building.

formal.uk: to escort someone from the premises
formal.us: to escort someone from the premises
formal.ex: Following the meeting, you [[were escorted from the premises]] and your access rights were withdrawn.

everyday.ex: Security [[walked him out]] in front of the whole floor, which was completely unnecessary.

informal.ex: She [[was marched out]] of the building like a criminal.

note_fr: « Premises » (toujours pluriel) = les locaux. Le verbe « to escort » est accentué sur la seconde syllabe. Pratique courante aux États-Unis ; en France, des circonstances humiliantes ou vexatoires peuvent ouvrir droit à des dommages-intérêts distincts, même si le licenciement est fondé.

def: A request, made within the company, for a more senior manager to review a disciplinary decision.

formal.ex: You have the right [[to appeal against the decision]] within five working days of receiving this letter.
formal.ex_us: You have the right [[to appeal the decision]] within five business days of receiving this letter.

everyday.ex: She's got a week [[to appeal]] if she thinks the warning is unfair.

note_fr: « To appeal against a decision » (UK), « to appeal a decision » (US, sans préposition). Offrir un recours interne est une exigence de bonne pratique au Royaume-Uni (code Acas) ; la loi française n'en prévoit pas, sauf convention collective ou règlement intérieur. « To appeal to someone » = plaire à quelqu'un !

def: To decide, after reviewing it, that an earlier decision was right and should stand.

formal.ex: Having considered your grounds of appeal, I have decided [[to uphold]] the original decision.

everyday.ex: The regional director [[stood by]] the warning.
everyday.ex_us: The regional director [[stuck with]] the warning.

note_fr: Piège : « to uphold a decision » = confirmer la décision (le salarié perd), mais « to uphold an appeal » ou « a complaint » = y faire droit (le salarié gagne). Verbe irrégulier : upheld. « To confirm » est possible, mais moins précis.

def: To decide that an earlier decision was wrong and cancel it.

formal.ex: The appeal manager [[overturned]] the dismissal and substituted a final written warning.

everyday.ex: They [[reversed]] the decision once the CCTV footage turned up.

collocations: to overturn a decision on appeal
note_fr: « To annul » est réservé au mariage et aux actes juridiques ; « to cancel » à un rendez-vous ou une commande. Pour une décision : « to overturn », « to reverse », ou « to quash » (plus juridique). « To substitute a lesser sanction » = prononcer une sanction moindre.

fr: licenciement pour motif valable (« for cause », États-Unis)
def: Termination based on a reason attributable to the employee, as defined in the contract or company policy, usually with loss of severance or other benefits.

formal.ex: In the event of [[termination for cause]], the Executive shall not be entitled to any severance payment.

everyday.ex: If he [[is dismissed for cause]], he walks away with nothing.
everyday.ex_us: If he [[is fired for cause]], he walks away with nothing.

note_fr: Notion contractuelle, surtout américaine : « cause » est défini clause par clause (fraude, condamnation, manquement grave...). Ne la confondez pas avec la cause réelle et sérieuse, exigée par la loi française pour tout licenciement. « Just cause » se rencontre dans les conventions collectives américaines.

fr: rupture sans motif à l'initiative de l'employeur (États-Unis)
def: Termination by the employer for no stated reason, which is lawful under the US at-will rule unless the real reason is an illegal one.

formal.ex: The Company may at any time [[terminate without cause]] the employment of any at-will employee.

everyday.uk: to let someone go without giving a reason
everyday.us: to let someone go without giving a reason
everyday.ex: In most US states you can [[let someone go without giving a reason]], but not for an illegal one.

note_fr: Inconcevable en France et, passé la période requise, au Royaume-Uni. « Without cause » ne signifie pas « sans risque » : discrimination et représailles restent interdites. À l'inverse, un client américain entendra « France requires cause » comme une contrainte très forte : prenez le temps de l'expliquer.
